flags: Dollar Tree completed the sale of the Family Dollar business to 1959 Holdings, LLC. Family Dollar results are reported as discontinued operations, and a transition services agreement continues.
Dollar Tree received $368.7 million of tariff refunds in the second quarter of fiscal 2026. This was the primary driver of the gross profit increase and of the jump in operating margin.
Dollar Tree announced a raised fiscal 2026 adjusted EPS outlook of $7.70 to $8.05. The range includes an approximate $0.60 benefit from the net impact of tariff refunds.

news.headline: Dollar Tree (DLTR) Q3 2026 Earnings Call Transcript
news.quote: Q3 comparable sales rose 4.6% and sales reached $5.1B; FY EPS guidance rises to $8.05-$8.25

touches.claim: Q2 profit was lifted by tariff refunds: diluted EPS of $2.70 included a $1.31 benefit, the operating margin gain included a 650 basis point refund benefit, and the full-year outlook still counts an approximate $0.60 refund benefit. Underlying earnings power is therefore smaller than the headline, and the refund boost may not repeat.

Traffic growth is thin and comparable sales growth depends mostly on average ticket. Q2 comps rose 3.7% with traffic up only 0.4%, and over six months traffic fell 0.3%. The 10-K said traffic declined in the last two quarters of fiscal 2025 after price changes. If price-led ticket growth fades, comps could slow.

Q3 results are due right after the decision time. The Q3 outlook has adjusted EPS of $0.80 to $0.95, including a $0.50 impact from tariff refund reinvestments, which sharply lowers the quarter's EPS from Q2's $2.70. A miss or a guide-down could change the reading of the year.
Dollar Tree is a scaled value retailer. It had 9,436 stores across the U.S. and Canada at the end of the second quarter of fiscal 2026, up from 9,282 at the start of the year.
Second-quarter sales growth was driven by both existing and new stores. Net sales rose 7.0% to $4,886.5 million, with comparable store net sales up 3.7%.
Customer traffic is only marginally positive. Q2 comparable sales rose on a 3.3% higher average ticket and 0.4% higher traffic, and traffic was down for the 26-week period.
The multi-price assortment is a differentiator that is being rolled out. About 710 stores were converted or added in Q2, ending the quarter with approximately 6,600 multi-price stores.

Management is reinvesting tariff refunds in the business, which dilutes near-term earnings. Q3 adjusted EPS guidance of $0.80 to $0.95 includes a $0.50 reinvestment impact, and full-year adjusted EPS guidance is $7.70 to $8.05.

Comparable store sales growth is a core driver. Q2 comps rose 3.7%, mostly from a 3.3% higher average ticket plus a 0.4% rise in traffic. For this to continue, traffic must hold up as ticket-raising pricing and mix changes are lapped.

Multi-price conversion is a driver of ticket and margin. The company converted or added about 710 stores in the quarter and ended with approximately 6,600 multi-price stores. For it to continue, customers must keep accepting prices above the $1.25 point, and labor and implementation costs must stay manageable.

Net new store and square-footage growth adds non-comparable sales. Stores rose to 9,436 from 9,148 a year earlier, and selling square footage grew 3.4%. Management plans approximately 400 openings and 75 closings this year. For this to continue, new sites must be found and opened on schedule at acceptable build-out cost.

Management guidance depends on the comp and margin conditions above: fiscal 2026 net sales of $20.5 billion to $20.7 billion on comps of 3% to 4%, and adjusted EPS of $7.70 to $8.05 including about $0.60 from net tariff refunds.

news.why: Dollar Tree beat Q3 FY2026 estimates with $5.1 billion in sales, 4.6% comparable sales growth, 3.8% traffic growth, 84 store openings, and easing multi-price backlash while raising full-year adjusted EPS guidance to $8.05-$8.25.

financial_health.claim: Working capital also contributed to operating cash flow. Accounts payable added 97.2 (table in millions), against an outflow of (114.0) a year earlier, and merchandise inventories released 40.2.

financial_health.basis: Stated in the cash flow statement and the earnings release. The funding link is inferred.
financial_health.claim: Cash is being returned to shareholders at a pace above free cash flow's growth in buybacks. Payments for repurchase of stock were 1,208.9 (table in millions) in the six months, and net cash used in financing was 723.8. The company reports $2.5 billion remaining under its repurchase authorization.

financial_health.basis: Stated for the borrowing balances and the earlier note repayment; the conclusion that pressure is low is inferred.
financial_health.claim: Near-term refinancing pressure looks low on the evidence given. The company reports no commercial paper and no revolver borrowings, and short-term borrowings were 0.0 (table in millions) against 299.5 a year earlier. The prior year already saw repayment of the $1.0 billion principal amount of 4.00% Senior Notes that were due May 15, 2025.
quotes: no commercial paper outstanding, and no borrowings under its revolving credit facility

financial_health.basis: Stated in the annual MD&A; the comparison with first-half spend is inferred.
financial_health.claim: Management points to operating cash flow, commercial paper and credit facilities as the way to fund planned spending. Capital expenditures for the current fiscal year are estimated at approximately $1.1 billion to $1.2 billion, against 498.8 (table in millions) spent in the first half.
quotes: from net cash provided by operations, our commercial paper program and borrowings under our credit facilities

growth_thesis.basis: Comp, ticket and traffic figures are stated in P6. The traffic condition is inferred from the P3 account of fiscal 2025.
growth_thesis.claim: Comparable store sales growth is a core driver. Q2 comps rose 3.7%, mostly from a 3.3% higher average ticket plus a 0.4% rise in traffic. For this to continue, traffic must hold up as ticket-raising pricing and mix changes are lapped.
quotes: Comparable store net sales increased 3.7%, driven by a 3.3% increase in average ticket and a 0.4% increase in traffic.
As a result of the retail price changes, customer traffic was negatively impacted and declined in the third and fourth quarters of fiscal 2025.

growth_thesis.basis: Store counts are stated in P6. The intent is stated in P3. The conditions are stated as risks in P2.
growth_thesis.claim: Multi-price conversion is a driver of ticket and margin. The company converted or added about 710 stores in the quarter and ended with approximately 6,600 multi-price stores. For it to continue, customers must keep accepting prices above the $1.25 point, and labor and implementation costs must stay manageable.
quotes: Converted or added about 710 stores to the Dollar Tree multi-price format, ending the quarter with approximately 6,600 multi-price stores

Our multi-price strategy is designed to increase basket size and drive margin expansion by introducing complementary products, new categories, larger pack sizes, and select branded and licensed items that we could not historically offer under a single price point.

growth_thesis.basis: Store counts and the outlook are stated in P6 and P4. The conditions are inferred from the P2 risk factors.
growth_thesis.claim: Net new store and square-footage growth adds non-comparable sales. Stores rose to 9,436 from 9,148 a year earlier, and selling square footage grew 3.4%. Management plans approximately 400 openings and 75 closings this year. For this to continue, new sites must be found and opened on schedule at acceptable build-out cost.
quotes: Approximately 400 new store openings and 75 closings

growth_thesis.basis: Stated in P4 and P6. The one-time character is inferred from the refund label and the guidance language.
growth_thesis.claim: Q2 gross profit rose 33.4% to $2,094.3 million, helped by $368.7 million of tariff refunds. That portion is a one-time benefit, so it is not a repeatable driver. Lasting margin growth requires the underlying drivers to persist: lower tariff rates, favorable shrink and occupancy leverage.
quotes: Gross profit increased 33.4% to $2,094.3 million primarily due to the receipt of $368.7 million of tariff refunds, the 3.7% comparable store net sales increase, our net store growth, lower tariff costs and improvements in shrink.
The remaining improvement in gross margin rate was primarily driven by lower tariff rates, favorable shrink, and occupancy leverage, partially offset by sales mix.

growth_thesis.basis: Share counts and authorization are stated in F2 and P6. The mechanism is inferred.
growth_thesis.claim: Share repurchases lift per-share results. Diluted weighted average shares for the quarter were 190.9 versus 207.8 a year earlier (shares in millions). For this to continue, cash generation and financing must keep funding buybacks, with $2.5 billion of authorization remaining.
quotes: As of August 1, 2026, the Company had $2.5 billion remaining under its share repurchase authorization, $1.1 billion of cash and cash equivalents, no commercial paper outstanding, and no borrowings under its revolving credit facility.
Q3 quarter-to-date share repurchases totaled $5.3 million

growth_thesis.basis: Figures are stated in F3. The sustainability condition is inferred from the line items.
growth_thesis.claim: Operating cash flow funds reinvestment and buybacks. Six-month net cash from continuing operations was 1,565.5 against 639.2 a year earlier, with capital expenditures of 498.8 (table in millions). For this to continue, working-capital inflows must not reverse. The year-to-date figure includes inflows from accounts payable of 97.2 and deferred taxes of 193.9.

growth_thesis.basis: Rates and amounts are stated in P6. The 18-month term is stated in P3. The replacement condition is inferred.
growth_thesis.claim: SG&A and corporate cost leverage supports profit growth. The Q2 SG&A rate fell to 29.2% from 29.6%, and corporate SG&A fell to $130.8 from $147.6 (table in millions). For this to continue, payroll savings must outweigh rising marketing and depreciation, and transition services income of $17.7 must be replaced once it ends.
quotes: The remaining year-over-year decrease primarily reflected lower payroll expenses partially offset by higher marketing and depreciation.

growth_thesis.basis: Stated in P3 and P2. Whether the Phoenix center opened on schedule is not stated in the packet.
growth_thesis.claim: Distribution-network expansion is intended to support growth, with the Phoenix center and a rebuilt Marietta, Oklahoma center as the named projects. For it to pay off, the openings must be completed on time, because delays could hurt product availability, sales and margins.
quotes: These investments are expected to support long-term growth and improve network resilience, though they may modestly impact gross margin in the near-to-mid term as capacity ramps up.

growth_thesis.basis: Stated in P6 as management outlook, not a result.
growth_thesis.claim: Management guidance depends on the comp and margin conditions above: fiscal 2026 net sales of $20.5 billion to $20.7 billion on comps of 3% to 4%, and adjusted EPS of $7.70 to $8.05 including about $0.60 from net tariff refunds.
quotes: Adjusted diluted EPS of $7.70 to $8.05 including an approximate $0.60 benefit related to the net impact of tariff refunds

material_events.claim: Dollar Tree completed the sale of the Family Dollar business to 1959 Holdings, LLC. Family Dollar results are reported as discontinued operations, and a transition services agreement continues.
quotes: On July 5, 2025, we completed our previously announced sale of the Family Dollar business to 1959 Holdings, LLC.

material_events.claim: Dollar Tree received $368.7 million of tariff refunds in the second quarter of fiscal 2026. This was the primary driver of the gross profit increase and of the jump in operating margin.
quotes: Gross profit increased 33.4% to $2,094.3 million primarily due to the receipt of $368.7 million of tariff refunds, the 3.7% comparable store net sales increase, our net store growth, lower tariff costs and improvements in shrink.

material_events.claim: Dollar Tree announced a raised fiscal 2026 adjusted EPS outlook of $7.70 to $8.05. The range includes an approximate $0.60 benefit from the net impact of tariff refunds.
quotes: Increasing fiscal 2026 adjusted EPS outlook to a range of $7.70 to $8.05 including an approximate $0.60 benefit related to the net impact of tariff refunds

material_events.basis: stated in the cash flow statement; the exact date within the six months is not given

quotes: Proceeds from long-term debt | 500.0 | 0.0

material_events.claim: Dollar Tree repurchased 11.1 million shares for $1.2 billion in the first half of fiscal 2026.
quotes: The Company repurchased 11.1 million shares for $1.2 billion, excluding applicable excise tax.

material_events.basis: stated in the cited item; the 8-K is dated November 3, 2026 and became public November 5, 2026

quotes: will report financial results for the third quarter of fiscal year 2026 ended on October 31, 2026, before the stock market opens on Tuesday, November 24, 2026

risks.basis: Stated in P6 and P4 (refund benefit amounts); the conclusion about repeatability is inferred.
risks.claim: Q2 profit was lifted by tariff refunds: diluted EPS of $2.70 included a $1.31 benefit, the operating margin gain included a 650 basis point refund benefit, and the full-year outlook still counts an approximate $0.60 refund benefit. Underlying earnings power is therefore smaller than the headline, and the refund boost may not repeat.
quotes: Diluted EPS of $2.70, including a $1.31 benefit related to the net impact of tariff refunds
Operating income margin expanded 900 basis points including a 650 basis point benefit related to the net impact of tariff refunds

risks.basis: Stated in P2 and P3 (uncertainty, volatility); the effect on margins is inferred from the risk-factor text.
risks.claim: Tariff policy remains unsettled. The 10-K says tariff volatility is expected to persist and that the availability, timing and amount of any further refunds are uncertain. New temporary tariffs followed the court ruling, so costs and margins could swing in either direction.
quotes: We expect tariff volatility to persist in the near-term, and implementation costs associated with our mitigation strategies may continue to be experienced before the benefits from those efforts are expected to materialize.
As a result, our margins and operating results could vary significantly.

risks.basis: Traffic and ticket figures are stated in P6 and P3; the risk to future comps is inferred.
risks.claim: Traffic growth is thin and comparable sales growth depends mostly on average ticket. Q2 comps rose 3.7% with traffic up only 0.4%, and over six months traffic fell 0.3%. The 10-K said traffic declined in the last two quarters of fiscal 2025 after price changes. If price-led ticket growth fades, comps could slow.
quotes: Net sales increased 7.0% to $4.9 billion. Comparable store net sales increased 3.7%, driven by a 3.3% increase in average ticket and a 0.4% increase in traffic.
Comparable store net sales increased 3.6%, driven by a 3.9% increase in average ticket, partially offset by a 0.3% decrease in traffic.
As a result of the retail price changes, customer traffic was negatively impacted and declined in the third and fourth quarters of fiscal 2025.

risks.basis: Outlook and release date are stated in P6 and P7; the risk of a miss is inferred.
risks.claim: Q3 results are due right after the decision time. The Q3 outlook has adjusted EPS of $0.80 to $0.95, including a $0.50 impact from tariff refund reinvestments, which sharply lowers the quarter's EPS from Q2's $2.70. A miss or a guide-down could change the reading of the year.
quotes: Q3 fiscal 2026 outlook of 3% to 4% comparable net sales growth and adjusted EPS of $0.80 to $0.95 including a $0.50 impact related to tariff refund reinvestments
will report financial results for the third quarter of fiscal year 2026 ended on October 31, 2026, before the stock market opens on Tuesday, November 24, 2026

risks.basis: SG&A amounts are stated in F2; the risk descriptions are stated in P2; the forward effect is inferred.
risks.claim: Costs and mix pressure persist. Q2 SG&A rose to 1,426.6 (table in millions) from 1,350.7 on higher marketing, depreciation and general liability costs, and the 10-K warns of wage, freight, labor and tariff cost pressure and a shift to lower-margin consumables. If sales growth slows, expense growth could squeeze margins.
quotes: Our profitability is vulnerable to cost pressures from increases in merchandise, shipping, freight and fuel, wages, benefits and other operating costs.
Over the past several years, we have experienced a shift in consumer purchasing from higher-margin discretionary merchandise to lower-margin consumable goods.

risks.basis: Balance sheet and cash flow figures are stated in F1 and F3; the risk is an inference and is weakly supported.
risks.claim: Balance sheet leverage has risen alongside heavy buybacks. In six months the company drew 500.0 (table in millions) of long-term debt and repurchased stock for 1,208.9. Long-term debt, net rose to 2,933.5 from 2,431.7 and shareholders' equity fell to 3,425.3 from 3,754.9. Large lease obligations add fixed commitments.
quotes: As of August 1, 2026, the Company had $2.5 billion remaining under its share repurchase authorization, $1.1 billion of cash and cash equivalents, no commercial paper outstanding, and no borrowings under its revolving credit facility.
